title: An initial functor induces an isomorphism of limits
statement: Let $H:\mathcal I\to\mathcal J$ be a functor between categories which is initial in the following sense: (1) for every object $y$ of $\mathcal J$ there are an object $x$ of $\mathcal I$ and a morphism $H(x)\to y$; (2) for every object $y$ of $\mathcal J$, all objects $x,x'$ of $\mathcal I$ and morphisms $a:H(x)\to y$, $a':H(x')\to y$ there are a sequence of morphisms $x=x_0\leftarrow x_1\rightarrow x_2\leftarrow x_3\rightarrow\cdots\rightarrow x_{2n}=x'$ in $\mathcal I$ and morphisms $a_i:H(x_i)\to y$ with $a_0=a$, $a_{2n}=a'$, such that $a_{2k}\circ H(x_{2k+1}\to x_{2k})=a_{2k+1}=a_{2k+2}\circ H(x_{2k+1}\to x_{2k+2})$ for $k=0,\ldots,n-1$. Let $\mathcal C$ be a category and $M:\mathcal J\to\mathcal C$ a functor. A *cone* on a functor $N:\mathcal K\to\mathcal C$ is an object $L$ with morphisms $p_k:L\to N(k)$ such that $N(b)\circ p_k=p_{k'}$ for every $b:k\to k'$; a *limit* of $N$ is a cone $(\varprojlim N,(p_k))$ through which every cone $(L',(p'_k))$ factors by exactly one morphism $L'\to\varprojlim N$. Then: (a) a cone $(L,(q_y)_y)$ on $M$ is a limit of $M$ if and only if its restriction $(L,(q_{H(x)})_x)$ is a limit of $M\circ H$; (b) every cone $(L,(p_x)_x)$ on $M\circ H$ is the restriction of a cone $(L,(q_y)_y)$ on $M$ with the same vertex. Consequently $M$ has a limit if and only if $M\circ H$ has one, and then the canonical morphism $\varprojlim_{\mathcal J}M\to\varprojlim_{\mathcal I}M\circ H$ (with components $q_{H(x)}$) is an isomorphism.
